claims.text: The starting material is an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy.
The starting alloy has a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
The proposed intervention is annealing at 250 °C for 10 hours.
Annealing at 250 °C for 10 hours will promote formation of a stable solid solution.
Annealing at 250 °C for 10 hours will reduce the amount of intermetallic phases.
Formation of a stable solid solution and reduction of intermetallic phases will improve room-temperature compressive behavior.
Formation of a stable solid solution and reduction of intermetallic phases will improve corrosion resistance.
Formation of a stable solid solution and reduction of intermetallic phases will improve resistance to high-temperature oxidation.
The improvements are predicted relative to the as-processed alloy.
The stated test-environment boundary is a controlled atmosphere.
The effect of annealing time and temperature on intermetallic-phase formation is uncertain.
The proposed falsification experiment anneals the alloy at 250 °C for 5 hours.
No improvement after a 5-hour anneal would falsify the hypothesis about a 10-hour anneal.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis concerns annealing for 10 hours, but the proposed falsification experiment uses 5 hours. Failure at 5 hours cannot decisively falsify the claimed effect at 10 hours.
